questions.question: Orient found 6 clusters that the pause constrains (trace `orient:`). What should this PR change beyond the RFC itself?

options.label: RFC + D3 cluster edits (Recommended)
options.description: RFC-0024 states the rule for open point 10 and a disposition per item for the D3 clusters. This PR then edits those backlog entries: about 25 items lose their "due before D3 step N" and get "paused by RFC-0024" or a re-scope. BK-485 goes to [~]. All other items are classified by the rule, not edited.

options.label: RFC only
options.description: The dispositions are recorded only in RFC-0024. BACKLOG.md changes only for BK-485. Until a follow-up sweep, the D3 items still say "due before D3 step 2", which contradicts the RFC (principle 3).

options.label: RFC + full backlog sweep
options.description: Every one of the ~120 open items gets a recorded disposition under the open-point-10 rule. The PR gets much larger and needs a long review.

questions.question: During the spec phase, where do 0.33 fixes land, and may the kernel already on master change?

options.label: Master first, kernel frozen (Recommended)
options.description: A 0.33 fix merges to master and is cherry-picked to release/0.33.x, so master's conformance suite stays the single record of 0.33 (D8). The kernel and Memory driver change only to keep the gates green. Their known defects, such as BK-450 T1, are recorded, not fixed.

options.label: Branch first, kernel frozen
options.description: Fixes land on release/0.33.x and are merged forward to master. Same kernel freeze. Master's suite trails the branch between merges.

options.label: Master first, kernel fixable
options.description: Same fix flow as the first option, but kernel defects (BK-450 T1 and the like) may also be fixed during the pause. That is production kernel code during the spec phase, which D3 rules out.

questions.question: What status does RFC-0024 land with, and does RFC-0017's Status change in this PR?

options.label: Accepted, RFC-0017 noted (Recommended)
options.description: D1 to D11 are already your decisions, so RFC-0024 lands Accepted. RFC-0017's Status gets one line, "D3 steps 2 to 8 paused by RFC-0024", in this PR (this answer is your confirmation). No ADR: D3 is process and lives in RFC-0017, not ADR-0042. release/0.33.x is cut after merge, when you confirm.

options.label: Accepted + ADR-0049
options.description: As the first option, plus an ADR recording D1, D7, D8 and D9, the parts that bind beyond process (behaviour may break; old specs are superseded; one 1.0.0 cut). It follows the pattern RFC-0022 set with ADR-0048.

options.label: Proposed, nothing else
options.description: RFC-0024 lands Proposed and RFC-0017 is untouched. Acceptance, the RFC-0017 note and the branch cut come in a follow-up PR.

questions.question: Open PR #1171 (BK-468) holds RFC-0023 and spec 054, a key spec built on spec 004 and 0.33 probes that overlaps step 4 (BK-484). How should RFC-0024 treat it?

options.label: Not ground; step 4 decides (Recommended)
options.description: RFC-0024 takes number 0024. It states that spec 054 was designed against 0.33 specs and probes, so it is not ground. Step 4 decides whether it becomes input to the key spec. #1171 stays open for you to decide.

options.label: Merge #1171 first; step 4 builds on it
options.description: Spec 054 becomes the base the key spec refines. That brings 0.33-grounded clauses into the new layer, against S1.

options.label: Leave it out of RFC-0024
options.description: No mention. The collision between #1171 and step 4 stays unrecorded until step 4.

questions.question: Open point 9: what form does a break record take, and how does it reach the migration guide?

options.label: One register, guide at implementation (Recommended)
options.description: A file `sdd/v1-breaks.md` holds one row per break: ID `BRK-NNN`, the v1 clause, the 0.33 behaviour with the test or spec ID that shows it, and what a caller changes. D8's comparison pass adds rows. The guide changes only when a break becomes real: that PR writes the `## v0.33 to v1.0.0` subsection and the `**Breaking**` entry under the existing rule, and the row links to it. Before the 1.0.0 cut, every row is either implemented or withdrawn.

options.label: Per-flow records, guide at the cut
options.description: Each operation's research doc lists its breaks. At the 1.0.0 cut, the migration guide is written from all of those docs. There is no central list, so the release checklist has to collect breaks across every flow.

options.label: Register + guide written as decided
options.description: Same register, but the guide's v1 section grows as each break is decided. master's dev docs would then publish breaks that no code makes yet, against principle 3.

questions.question: A v1 spec will disagree with 0.33 code until implementation. 000-process Rule 3 says the code is then wrong. How does this PR handle that?

options.label: Amend 000-process Rule 3 now (Recommended)
options.description: Rule 3 gains one sentence: a spec the ground register lists binds code only once its implementation begins. Until then, a difference from 0.33 is a break record or a 0.33 bug (D8). CLAUDE.md is untouched, so the process budget needs no raise; its principle 5 already defers to 000-process.

options.label: Rule 3 + CLAUDE.md principle 5
options.description: Same sentence, plus a clause in CLAUDE.md principle 5 so a session sees the rule without opening 000-process. Needs a recorded process-budget raise.

options.label: Defer to step 3
options.description: The RFC states the rule, and the amendment lands when the ground register exists. Until then, the accepted RFC and Rule 3 disagree on paper; spec 051 is the only case today.

questions.question: What does "fixes only" admit on release/0.33.x?

options.label: Patch-bump changes (Recommended)
options.description: Whatever CONTRIBUTING § When to bump rates patch or no bump: bug fixes, patch-eligible floor raises, CI, docs and metadata. So BK-409's 3.15 classifier is in if no code changes. Anything rated minor is refused on the branch.

options.label: Bug fixes and security only
options.description: No floor raises, no classifier or CI changes. The 0.33 line freezes its support matrix at v0.33.0.

options.label: Fixes + support additions
options.description: Also new interpreters and floor raises that would rate minor. They ship as 0.33.x patches, which bends semver for those changes.

When is `release/0.33.x` created and pushed from the v0.33.0 tag?

options.label: Now, before the PR (Recommended)
options.description: I run `git branch release/0.33.x v0.33.0` and push it, with no commits on it. The PR can then describe a branch that exists (principle 3), and CONTRIBUTING gets its patch-release route in this PR. Branch protection and the CI triggers come later: v0.33.0's ci.yml runs only for master, so the first PR into the branch has to add itself to the triggers. RFC-0024 states this.

options.label: After the PR merges
options.description: The PR records the cut as decided but not done. CONTRIBUTING's patch-release route and BK-485's "done" wording wait for a follow-up commit.

options.label: Not until a fix needs it
options.description: The branch is cut the first time a 0.33 fix has to ship. Until then, RFC-0024 states the rule with no branch behind it.

questions.question: BK-456 ([~], two stages merged this week) plans stage three: pruning spec 003 against SPEC-DESIGN.md. D7 supersedes old specs section by section rather than reworking them. What happens to stage three?

options.label: Park stage three (Recommended)
options.description: BK-456 stays [~], and its entry says stage three is paused by RFC-0024 D7: spec 003 is superseded by the v1 flows, not pruned. Its contradictions stay recorded in audit 024 as input for the comparison pass. If another session is working on stage three now, that work stops.

options.label: Keep stage three
options.description: The prune goes ahead. It makes spec 003 a cleaner record of 0.33 for fix work on the 0.33 line, at the cost of reworking a spec D7 will retire.

options.label: Close BK-456 as done
options.description: The two shipped stages close it, and stage three goes to § Decided against with D7 as the reason.

questions.question: BK-450 T1 (returned metadata is the live stored dict) is measured on released v0.33.0 Memory as well as on master's kernel. On master, fixing it means touching the frozen kernel. How should the rule treat a 0.33 defect that also lives in the kernel?

options.label: Defect exception to the freeze (Recommended)
options.description: The freeze admits a fix to a defect a released 0.33 version has. On master the fix goes into the kernel or Memory driver; on release/0.33.x it is ported to the hand-written class, since a cherry-pick cannot apply. No new kernel features. T1 then becomes a 0.33 defect with its own item, split out of BK-450, and the rest of BK-450 is parked.

options.label: Branch-only fix, kernel keeps it
options.description: The fix lands only on release/0.33.x. Master's kernel keeps the defect, recorded in BK-450 (parked), until D10. This breaks the master-first rule for this class of defect.

options.label: Record only, fix nowhere
options.description: T1 stays in parked BK-450 as a known defect on both lines. The 0.33 line ships it unfixed.
